<thought>Using the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 233.9632, which corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.0073 Da) gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 232.956 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a prominent M+2 peak (~24 % of the base peak), characteristic of a single chlorine atom. Accounting for one ³⁵Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves a remaining mass of ≈ 197.987 Da to be composed of C, H, O and N. The combination that best matches this residual mass is C₁₂H₈ClNO₂, whose calculated exact mass (232.956 Da) matches the observed neutral mass within experimental error. Therefore the molecular formula of the compound is C12H8ClNO2.</thought>
<final_answer>C12H8ClNO2</final_answer>
